speaker: Brick Bronson
before: NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER. I AM THE SPOTTER.
after: STOP RIGHT THERE! NOBODY CROSSES THE GORGE WITHOUT A SPOTTER, AND I AM THE SPOTTER, AND I AM NOT SPOTTING ANYBODY ACROSS IT TODAY!

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: THE BRIDGE STAYS UP BY ORDER OF CHANCELLOR CLENCH! ONLY IRON MATTERS! ...AND HYDRATION! (quieter) The regime is very big on hydration.
after: THE BRIDGE STAYS UP BY ORDER OF CHANCELLOR CLENCH, BECAUSE ONLY IRON MATTERS! IRON AND HYDRATION! (quieter) The regime is very big on hydration, so do drink something while you're waiting.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN IT! TEN REPS, NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING AND I FEEL FANTASTIC!
after: IF YOU WANT THIS CRANK YOU WILL HAVE TO EARN IT, TEN REPS AND NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING AND I FEEL FANTASTIC! ...I THINK IT IS FANTASTIC. MY KNEES STOPPED TELLING ME THINGS.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: HYDRATION BREAK. NOBODY LIFTS DURING HYDRATION. THAT IS THE LAW. ...It is a good law.
after: HYDRATION BREAK! NOBODY LIFTS DURING HYDRATION, AND THAT IS THE LAW! ...It is a good law.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT! THE BRIDGE STAYS UP, AND SO DO I! NEITHER OF US IS ALLOWED TO SIT DOWN!
after: COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT, AND I WILL BE RIGHT HERE, BECAUSE THE BRIDGE STAYS UP AND SO DO I! NEITHER OF US HAS BEEN ALLOWED TO SIT DOWN IN A VERY LONG TIME!

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Shh, keep it down - the regime has big ears up here. Welcome to the Gainlands. They call me Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its people moving... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.
after: Shh, keep it down, the regime has big ears up here. Welcome to the Gainlands. They call me Old Man Mountain, and we Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its people moving, and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge - Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil, if you can believe it. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight. Every... every last plate.
after: Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge, and he was Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil, if you can believe it. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight, to the last plate.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: We're tired, but we haven't crumbled. If you fall, I'll catch you: rule one, never lift alone. Rule two, never skip leg day. Rule three is... I've forgotten rule three. Two's plenty.
after: We're tired, but we haven't crumbled, and if you fall I'll catch you. That's rule one, never lift alone. Rule two, never skip leg day. Rule three is... I've forgotten rule three. Two's plenty.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: And that gate up on the overlook, past the ridge, won't budge for anybody. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.
after: Now, where was I? The gate, that's it. The one up on the overlook, past the ridge, won't budge for anybody. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely, twice.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Back again? Good. The only bad rep is the one nobody was there to spot.
after: Back again? Good, good, come and stand where I can see you. I always say the only bad rep is the one nobody was there to spot.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: You beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes. Even the illegal flavour. Especially the illegal flavour... ah, I can nearly taste it.
after: You beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes, even the illegal flavour. Especially the illegal flavour, come to think of it... ah, I can nearly taste it.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Foreman Gus. I keep the wheels turning, the grid humming and the hamsters - sorry, the volunteers - fed. They put pre-workout in the water. So far I'm mostly feeling the water.
after: I'm Foreman Gus. I keep the wheels turning and the grid humming, and I keep the hamsters fed - the volunteers, I'm meant to call them. The regime puts pre-workout in the water, and so far I'm mostly feeling the water.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels only go to a hundred. The extra ten comes out of the crew, and nobody writes down where it went.
after: The regime wants a hundred and ten percent out of us, and the wheels only go to a hundred. The extra ten comes out of the crew, and nobody writes down where it went.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The crews on the city wheels up in the Capital have it worse. They're told it's cardio, for their own good. It's neither.
after: The crews on the city wheels up in the Capital have it worse than we do. They're told it's cardio, and that it's for their own good, and it isn't either one.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: LET'S GO! A NEW RECRUIT! Coach Brutus Benchley - retired champion, current motivator, part-time merchant! Protein, powder and pasteboard! SUPPLEMENTS FOR YOUR DECK!
after: LET'S GO! A NEW RECRUIT! I'm Coach Brutus Benchley, retired champion and full-time motivator, and I sell cards on the side, because a deck needs its SUPPLEMENTS the same as you do!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: REGIME-APPROVED MERCHANDISE! Not actually approved, but these old cards have a GREAT ATTITUDE!
after: IT'S ALL REGIME-APPROVED MERCHANDISE! Well, nobody actually approved it, champ, but these old cards have a GREAT ATTITUDE, and I'd put any one of them in my starting line-up!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: *whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter. There's nothing under it. Just some iron, which officially doesn't exist.
after: *whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter, would you? There's nothing under it. Only a bit of iron, and officially that doesn't exist.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are pumped and my whistle's been SAVING ITS BREATH for you!
after: LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are warmed up and stretched, champ, and my whistle's been SAVING ITS BREATH for you all day!

speaker: Gary
before: Mmmph! Oh, thank goodness, a spotter! Hi, I'm Gary. Lovely to meet you. Sorry I can't shake hands.
after: Mmmph! Oh, thank goodness, a spotter! Hi, I'm Gary, it's lovely to meet you, and I'm so sorry I can't get up to shake hands.

speaker: Gary
before: I've been under this barbell since lunch. Possibly since the regime took over - it's hard to tell from down here. No rush. Bit of a rush.
after: I've been under this barbell since lunch, or possibly since the regime took over, it's hard to tell from down here. There's no rush at all. Well, there's a bit of a rush.

speaker: Gary
before: It's the last barbell they didn't confiscate, so I got excited and loaded one more plate than my confidence.
after: It's the last barbell they didn't confiscate, you see, so I got excited and loaded one more plate than I had the confidence for.

speaker: Gary
before: It's fine. It's FINE. Could you give it a little push? Whenever you're ready. Now would be good.
after: It's fine, honestly, it's FINE. Could you possibly give it a little push, though? Whenever you're ready, I don't want to be a bother. Now would be good.

speaker: Gary
before: Spotter, you're a hero! One day this barbell and I will rise to the occasion... with you watching, please.
after: Oh, it's my spotter! You're a hero, you really are. One of these days this barbell and I are going to rise to the occasion, and I'd be very grateful if you were standing nearby when we try.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The lights keep flickering because the regime pipes every watt up to the House of Gains. Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill and we'll keep a little for ourselves. Call it quiet resistance.
after: The lights keep flickering because the regime pipes every watt we make up to the House of Gains. If you'd run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill for me, we could keep a little down here. Call it quiet resistance.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. It's for crew morale. Mostly mine.
after: After that, buy yourself a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. It's for crew morale, and I'll be honest with you, mostly mine.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. Come and find me when you're done.
after: Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station, and come and find me when you've done both.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The Swole Station's lights are back on and the grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Here, take your reward.
after: The Swole Station's lights are back on and the grid's humming. I'd make a speech about it, but all my energy went into the lights, so here, take your reward instead.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Don't let the hamsters hear you call them 'volunteers'. They're sensitive.
after: And don't let the hamsters hear you call them 'volunteers'. They're sensitive about it.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The grid's running smooth, and some of the power's even staying here for once. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman, so I'll nod. ...That was a big nod, for me.
after: The grid's running smooth, and some of the power's even staying here for once. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman, so you get a nod. ...That was a big nod, for me.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Which brings me back to rule one. Gary's stuck under a barbell again - follow the groaning and give him a spot. Then check your form at a Flex Mirror. The regime tried confiscating reflections once. It didn't take.
after: Which brings me back to rule one. Gary's stuck under a barbell again, so follow the groaning and give him a spot, then check your form at a Flex Mirror. The regime tried confiscating reflections once, and it didn't take.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Do both and I'll have Shredna rip you a portal out to Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months, and the calves... well, you'll see.
after: Do both and I'll have Shredna rip you a portal out to Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months, and the calves... well, you'll see for yourself.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Spot Gary at his barbell, then flex at a Flex Mirror: the one at the Station or the one up on Pec Perch. Spot first, flex second, brag third.
after: Spot Gary at his barbell, then flex at a Flex Mirror, either the one at the Station or the one up on Pec Perch. Spot first and flex second, that's the order, and you can brag to me about it afterwards.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: You spotted Gary and checked your form? Beautiful. Here, have a Pre-Workout Jitters, on the house.
after: You spotted Gary and you checked your form? Beautiful, that's just how it's meant to be done. Here, have a Pre-Workout Jitters, on the house.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Calf Cove's open to you now. Tell Shredna I said hello. She'll pretend she didn't miss me.
after: And Calf Cove's open to you now. Say hello to Shredna for me when you go through, would you? She'll pretend she hasn't missed me, she always does.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Calf Cove's yours now. Mind the edge out there - always mind the edge. I didn't, once, back in the spring of... never mind.
after: Calf Cove's yours now. Mind the edge out there, though, always mind the edge. I didn't, once, back in the spring of... oh, never mind, it was a long time ago and I bounced.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep EATING my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM! I WRITE IT ON EVERY LID!
after: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep EATING my deliveries, champ! I need you to beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM! I WRITE IT ON EVERY LID!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: I'll pay you in cards! STRONG cards! *whispering* Heavy ones. The kind the regime hasn't found yet.
after: And I'll pay you in cards, STRONG cards! *whispering* Heavy ones, the kind the regime hasn't found yet.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: Three roaming enemies out in the Gainlands, champ! The brutes flex! The golems rattle!
after: That's three roaming enemies out in the Gainlands, champ, any three you fancy! The brutes flex at you and the golems rattle!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: The sprites buzz! Pick your poison and GET OUT THERE!
after: And the sprites buzz, which is the worst of the lot if you ask me! So pick your poison and GET OUT THERE!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: THREE DOWN! Deliveries are BACK ON SCHEDULE! Here, take a Leg Day for your trouble, and do NOT skip it, champ! I mean that as a coach AND as a card dealer!
after: THREE DOWN, and my deliveries are BACK ON SCHEDULE! Here, take a Leg Day for your trouble, and do NOT skip it, champ! I'm telling you that as a coach AND as a card dealer!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: The lanes are clear! For about an hour! Then the regime fills them up again! BUT WHAT AN HOUR!
after: The lanes are clear, champ! They'll stay clear for about an hour, and then the regime will fill them right back up again, BUT WHAT AN HOUR!

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring, don't mind me. Lovely broad shoulders up here - very roomy work, when it comes. Not that it's come lately. Heh.
after: Just measuring, don't mind me. Lovely broad shoulders you all have up here, so it'll be nice roomy work when it comes. Not that any of it's come lately, mind. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see, you're... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's have a look for you, shall we... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! You carry on, then, and mind your back around all this lifting. Heh.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: And you walked in at a pace of seven out of ten. Disappointing, but at least it's measurable.
after: As for you, you entered at a walking pace of seven out of ten. That is disappointing, but it is at least measurable, which is more than I can say for most visitors.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Who are you?
after: You're the first person in this place who hasn't shouted at me. Who are you?

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency. I designed the wheels, the schedules and the prison downstairs. The Chancellor does the shouting. I do the arithmetic.
after: I am Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency. I designed the wheels, the schedules and the prison downstairs. The Chancellor does the shouting, and I do the arithmetic.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Hold still while I measure you. Grip, low. Stride, uneven. Resolve... unusually high, and that is an inefficiency I intend to remove.
after: Hold still, please, while I measure you. Your grip is low and your stride is uneven. Your resolve, however, is unusually high, and that is an inefficiency I intend to remove.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Your performance: forty-one percent of acceptable. Mine is about to improve.
after: Your performance stands at forty-one percent of acceptable. Mine is about to improve.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Ninety-four seconds. You beat me in ninety-four seconds.
after: Ninety-four seconds. You defeated me in ninety-four seconds, and I had allowed three hundred for the reverse.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: I'll note it, the way I note everything. The Chancellor is not going to enjoy this figure.
after: I shall note it, as I note everything. That is not a compliment. I simply cannot leave a figure unsaid, and the Chancellor is not going to enjoy this one.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: "You carry the whole kingdom in your lungs, son. Try not to drop it."
after: "There. You have been holding that breath since long before you came down my stairs, son, and you needn't. The climb will still be here when you have let it out."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: CUT THE POWER. Everyone off the wheels. Nobody moves unless I say REP.
after: CUT THE POWER and get everyone off the wheels! Nobody in this house moves a muscle until I say REP!

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: You said I would go further than you. Look how far I went. ...Master?
after: You told me I would go further than you ever did. Well, look how far I went. Tell me it was far enough. ...Master?

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "A stranger in my house, and no old man at your side. They say Flex is still down in the dark, doing push-ups for nobody."
after: "A stranger in my house, and you didn't even bring the old man up with you. They tell me Flex is still down there in the dark, doing push-ups for nobody."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "They say he trained a hundred pupils and I was the best of them. Look where that got me. Look where it got him."
after: "They say he trained a hundred pupils and that I was the best of them. Well, look where being the best got me, and then look where teaching got him."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "Come, then. Let me show you what iron is for."
after: "Step up to the bench, then, stranger, and let me show you what iron is for."

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: "I was going to leave eventually," he says. "Lovely day for it." Then he looks at his fallen pupil, and his face softens.
after: "I heard the cheering, and I thought it was time I came up," he says. "Lovely day for it." Then he looks at his fallen pupil, and his face softens.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: "Get up, my boy. We start from zero. Everyone does."
after: "Up you get, my boy. We'll start again from zero, the way everyone does."

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: You did it! Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch the whole thing. Best day since... oh, since the last best day, whenever that was. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
after: You did it! Flex is out and Clench is down, and I got to watch the whole thing from the good bench. Best day since... oh, since the last best day, whenever that was. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Weights back in the gym, and there's Gary, lifting with a proper spotter. Beautiful. Before you go... that boy I told you about, the old king's son, at the Festival...
after: The weights are back in the gym, and there's Gary over there, lifting with a proper spotter at last. Beautiful. Now, before you go... that boy I told you about, the old king's son, up at the Festival...

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Free, strong and properly spotted, all of us. Thank you, friend. I climbed Swolympus once, you know, and these ten years were steeper.
after: We're free and strong and properly spotted, every one of us, and that's your doing, friend. I climbed Swolympus once, you know, back when my knees and I were on speaking terms, and these ten years were steeper.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: That gate up on the overlook is still sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.
after: That gate up on the overlook is still sealed, mind. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely again this morning, which makes three times.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Foreman Gus, still on the wheels. But listen to them now - not a single whistle.
after: Foreman Gus, still on the wheels. But listen to them now. They're turning, and there isn't a single whistle blowing over them.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The grid's at a hundred percent, and nobody wants ten more. Turns out a hundred was all of it.
after: The grid's at a hundred percent and nobody's asking for ten more. Turns out a hundred was all of it, the whole time.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: I might even take a day off. No idea how it's done, but I hear you start by sitting down.
after: I might even take a day off. I've no idea how it's done, but I'm told you start by sitting down.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The wheels turn when they feel like it, and somehow we've never had more power. I'd tell the regime, but there isn't one.
after: The wheels turn when the crew feels like turning them, and somehow we've never had more power. I'd report it to the regime, but there isn't one.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: LET'S GO! The iron came out from under the floorboard and went STRAIGHT onto a rack! Benchley's is open to EVERYONE!
after: LET'S GO! The iron came out from under the floorboard and went STRAIGHT onto a rack where everybody can see it! Benchley's is open to EVERYONE, champ, and that's the best line-up I've ever fielded!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: REGIME MERCHANDISE IN THE CLEARANCE BIN! Nobody wants it - my proudest day of not making a sale!
after: ALL THE REGIME MERCHANDISE IS IN THE CLEARANCE BIN! Nobody wants any of it, and I have never been so proud of not making a sale!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: CARDS ON SHELVES, IRON ON RACKS! And I don't have to whisper about the floorboard any more, which is good, because I WAS NEVER ANY GOOD AT IT!
after: CARDS ON THE SHELVES AND IRON ON THE RACKS! And I don't have to whisper about the floorboard any more, which is just as well, because I WAS NEVER ANY GOOD AT IT!

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Welcome, friend. Grandmaster Flex, at your service. After ten years in the dark, the first thing I wanted was a window, and the second was a good long stretch.
after: Welcome, son, welcome. Grandmaster Flex, at your service, and it is good to say so in daylight. After ten years in the dark, the first thing I wanted was a window, and the second was a good long stretch.
